text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Bunds, futures slightly down in late dealings as market awaits U.S. data on Tuesday. Little movement was seen in meantime amid consolidation after last week's turbulence. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.12, down 0.02 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts edged lower in afternoon trade and underperformed gilts as the prospect of 2.5 billion sterling ($4.06 billion) of new 10-year gilts coming Tuesday weighed on the market. Traders said auction should go well and short tail could prompt rally. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-09/32, down 09/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - March bond future settles at lows, U.S. bonds weighing later. Volume subdued. Focus remains on U.S. employment cost data due Tuesday. BoF left rates steady as expected. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.14 down 0.18 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and futures ended in positive territory but were soggy and not far off session lows in a quiet, directionless market looking to the U.S. for impetus. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 131.56 up 0.11 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries still hurt in thin late morning trade. Players seen mostly sidelined ahead of key Q4 ECI Tuesday. Market shows little reaction to Dec existing home sales data. Flows very light. Market psychology remains negative. Retailers, hedge funds sidelined. Dealer trade dominates.The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-31/32, down 9/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.92 percent.

JAPAN - Key March Japanese goverment bonds (JGB) futures contract ended Monday sharply higher, retaining bullishness after it hit record high of 126.83. Contract jumped after round of speculative buying buoyed SIMEX during Tokyo lunch break. Short-covering continued as contract broke above key resistance points.In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.57, up 0.38 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market got the week off to a steady start with a good mix of new issues. SuedwestLB launched a $750 million five-year via CSFB and Goldman Sachs, a repeat of a deal launched last October. Today's spread was 10 bp, against the prior deal's 14 bp. British property firm Land Securities set a 200 million stg 10-year convertible. Deutsche Bank issued a self-led 20 billion drachma bond. BIL set a 1.0 billion Czech crown one-year Eurobond.
